# E4d — where the time goes in six flow-matching VLAs, and what moves it

**Generated by `bench/make_phase_report.py` from the committed result rows.** Every number here is re-derived from `results/*/raw/rows/*.json` at generation time; none is typed in, so the prose cannot drift from the measurements when a rung is re-run.

Device: Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB, MAXN, 16 SMs, GPU pinned 1300.5 MHz, JetPack 6.2.3 / L4T R36.5.0 / CUDA 12.6, sm_87. Measured peaks (T005/E1): 187.47 GB/s, 33.85 TFLOP/s bf16, ridge **180.57 FLOP/B**.

## 1. The question: which models are action-head bottlenecked?

Each model gets an identical treatment — the same one-factor ladder, at its own configured N, with the phase split taken by compiling first and instrumenting afterwards so no region boundary falls inside a compiled graph.

| model | N | action head, eager | action head, best | e2e eager (ms) | e2e best (ms) | overall speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| π0 | 10 | 54.9 % | 39.7 % (`bf16_both`) | 1069.04 | 424.46 (`bf16_both`) | 2.52× |
| π0.5 | 10 | 20.4 % | 38.2 % (`bf16_both`) | 3028.56 | 489.15 (`bf16_both`) | 6.19× |
| SmolVLA | 10 | 85.3 % | 48.6 % (`vlm_graphs`) | 727.46 |  80.97 (`whole_graphs`) | 8.98× |
| GR00T N1.7 | 4 | 56.7 % | 33.1 % (`vlm_compile`) | 372.48 | 240.49 (`vlm_compile`) | 1.55× |
| GR00T N1.6 | 4 | 61.5 % | 39.5 % (`vis_compile`) | 327.22 | 186.12 (`vis_compile`) | 1.76× |
| GR00T N1.5 | 4 | 38.6 % | 31.0 % (`vlm_compile`) | 255.22 | 200.85 (`vlm_compile`) | 1.27× |

**Two shares, at the SAME N.** π0's directory holds both an N = 10 ladder and an N = 4 control, and an earlier version of this generator keyed rows by rung alone, so the N = 4 rows silently overwrote the N = 10 ones. That produced a perfectly plausible table in which π0 appeared to fall to 18.9 % — which is its N = 4 figure. At its configured N = 10 it falls to 39.7 %. Every row above is filtered to one N.

π0 as a within-model control on N, both ends measured identically:

| π0 | eager e2e | AE share, eager | best (with split) | AE share, best |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| N = 4 | 711.75 ms | 32.3 % | `vlm_graphs` 369.51 ms | 18.7 % |
| N = 10 | 1069.04 ms | 54.9 % | `bf16_both` 424.46 ms | 39.7 % |

Same model, same machine, only N changes: the action-head share nearly doubles at both ends of the ladder. N matters — it is simply not the *only* thing that matters, which the GR00T family shows.

**The prediction recorded before these runs was wrong.** The plan predicted that action-head dominance would track the denoising step count N far more than architecture, putting the GR00T family lowest because it uses N = 4. It does not: N1.6 and N1.7 at N = 4 sit *above* π0 at N = 10. The reason is in the checkpoints — N1.6 and N1.7 carry **32** DiT blocks and N1.5 carries **16** (C3, `bench/expert_dims.py`), so within one family at one N the share moves with the size of the head. Architecture dominates step count.

## 3. Which lever moved which phase

Best measured value per phase, against that model's eager baseline.

| model | vision eager → best | vlm_prefix eager → best | action head eager → best |
|---|---|---|---|
| π0 | 241.0 → **56.7** (4.25×, `bf16_both`) | 234.6 → **192.8** (1.22×, `vlm_compile`) | 586.9 → **168.7** (3.48×, `bf16_both`) |
| π0.5 | 239.5 → **56.7** (4.22×, `bf16_both`) | 2162.5 → **239.5** (9.03×, `bf16_both`) | 617.7 → **186.7** (3.31×, `bf16_both`) |
| SmolVLA | 33.3 → **31.2** (1.07×, `vlm_compile`) | 65.8 → **7.9** (8.30×, `vlm_graphs`) | 620.6 → **43.6** (14.22×, `vis_compile`) |
| GR00T N1.7 | 70.6 → **70.1** (1.01×, `eager_tf32`) | 88.6 → **87.1** (1.02×, `ae_compile`) | 211.1 → **79.5** (2.66×, `ae_graphs`) |
| GR00T N1.6 | 61.9 → **46.8** (1.32×, `vis_compile`) | 61.7 → **51.2** (1.21×, `vlm_graphs`) | 201.3 → **73.0** (2.76×, `ae_graphs`) |
| GR00T N1.5 | 50.2 → **35.1** (1.43×, `vis_compile`) | 100.6 → **78.8** (1.28×, `vlm_compile`) | 98.5 → **61.9** (1.59×, `vis_compile`) |

Two things this table is for. First, **precision beats compilation on the VLM prefix for π0.5**: compiling moved it 534 → 516 ms (1.04×) while casting the fp32 checkpoint to bf16 moved it 516 → 239 ms (2.16×). Second, **CUDA graphs on the prefix are model-dependent, not a general win** — a 2× gain on SmolVLA and a net loss on π0 and π0.5, which is consistent with π0's prefix being compute-bound at 816 FLOP/B while SmolVLA's is small enough to be launch-bound.

## 4. Not measured, and why

| model | rung | reason |
|---|---|---|
| π0 | `bf16_base` | not applicable — checkpoint already loads bf16 (config dtype=bfloat16), so there is no fp32 base to cast |
| SmolVLA | `bf16_base` | not applicable — checkpoint already loads bf16 (config dtype=bfloat16), so there is no fp32 base to cast |
| SmolVLA | `bf16_both` | not applicable — SmolVLAPolicy has no fp32 vision island: LeRobot loads its vision tower in bf16 already, so there is nothing for B2 to remove |
| SmolVLA | `bf16_norms` | not applicable — SmolVLAPolicy has no params_to_keep_float32: its norms are not held in fp32, so there is nothing for B3 to cast |
| SmolVLA | `bf16_vision` | not applicable — SmolVLAPolicy has no fp32 vision island: LeRobot loads its vision tower in bf16 already, so there is nothing for B2 to remove |
| GR00T N1.7 | `vis_compile` | failed — TorchRuntimeError: Dynamo failed to run FX node with fake tensors: call_function flash_attn._flash_attn_varlen_forward(*(FakeTensor(..., device='cuda: |

A blank cell in this report is always one of these two rows, never silence. `not applicable` means the rung cannot exist for that model — SmolVLA ships its VLM in bf16 already, so there is no fp32 island for B2/B3 to remove — and `failed` means it was attempted and did not run, with the error kept.
